tier_reason: README chart (images/perfgraphs.png) gives first-party numbers against Embree and madmann91/bvh, produced by the public tiny_bvh_benchmark.cpp, which builds both baselines; no CPU model, compiler or flags are stated for the CPU chart, so it is C, not A. Upgraded from D because the chart does carry numeric axes.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart (approximate readings from bar chart): Sponza 263k-tri 'fast build' BVH build ~6.7 ms vs Embree ~17.5 ms and Madmann91 ~13 ms (~2.6x vs Embree, derived from page data); single-core CPU traversal nearest-hit ~16 vs Embree ~6.2 and MM91 ~2.3 MRay/s; any-hit ~36 vs Embree ~23.5 MRay/s. Author calls results 'preliminary'.
corrections.workload: SAH BVH build (Crytek Sponza, 263k triangles) and single-core single-ray nearest-hit/any-hit traversal on CPU vs Embree and madmann91/bvh; separately GPU traversal up to 5 billion rays/s on Sponza (RTX 5080 laptop, no baseline).
corrections.caveats: Author labels results 'preliminary' and notes single-ray traversal is only a small part of Embree (Embree's packet/stream paths not compared). Chart numbers are bar readings; no CPU model, compiler or flags given. Baseline Embree is a ray-tracing incumbent, not one of the category's listed baselines (Boost.Geometry/CGAL/GEOS).

notes: Benchmark code: tiny_bvh_benchmark.cpp (Experiment entries for EMBREE and MADMANN91). Widely used (Remedy Northlight, Houdini). Metadata confirmed: MIT, 1.2k stars, last commit 2026-09-25, not archived/fork. Shortcoming to record: off-category baseline, no hardware/flags.
